concepts.why: The patient's presentation with a large polypoid mass obstructing the left nasal cavity, combined with the presence of CD138-positive, CD56-positive, and EBV-positive cells, and gains of florescence signal at multiple loci, is consistent with Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type.

The patient's presentation with a large polypoid mass obstructing the left nasal cavity, combined with the gains of florescence signal at multiple loci, including 3q27 (BCL6) and 14q32 (IGH), is consistent with Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
The patient's presentation with a large polypoid mass obstructing the left nasal cavity, combined with the presence of CD138-positive cells, is consistent with Plasma cell neoplasm.

The patient's presentation with a 12-month history of left-sided nasal congestion and obstruction, combined with the presence of a large polypoid mass obstructing the left nasal cavity, is consistent with Nasal polyp.
It explains the CD20-negative and PAX5-negative findings in the context of a lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation, as suggested by the CD138-positive and CD56-positive results.
